sentences.text: Paraplesiobatis was a lightly armored placoderm, an ancient fish with bony plates, belonging to the order Pseudopetalichthyida.
The single known specimen measures 10 centimeters in total length and includes a plate-covered head and part of the vertebral column.
The genus Paraplesiobatis was described by Broili in 1933.
The only known species is Paraplesiobatis heinrichsi.
Experts suggest that Paraplesiobatis may belong to the same genus or species as Pseudopetalichthys due to strong resemblance.
Paraplesiobatis lived in Early Devonian Germany.
It lived during the Emsian stage, between 410.62 and 399.5 million years ago.
It is debated whether Paraplesiobatis and Pseudopetalichthys are the same, but a decision cannot be made until better preserved specimens are discovered.
